summary: Current 1961 Washington DNR live-in cab, replacing a 1934 L-4 pole tower; damaged in the 2015 Okanogan Complex fire and repaired; kept for emergency use.

facts.design: 14 by 14 foot flat-gable Washington DNR live-in cab on a 20-foot timber tower (current structure)

access.note: The road is on state land and is rough. The DNR cab is kept for emergency use and the catwalk is usually locked.

visit.trail_note: Rough road; high clearance and four-wheel drive recommended. TrailChick lists a 3.9-mile round trip.

events.note: Crow's nest and log cabin developed by the state. Will Hite and TrailChick give about 1911 for the first lookout.
Fred Cole assigned to staff the cabin for the 1920 fire season
20-foot pole tower with L-4 cab; TrailChick says it replaced the crow's nest and cabin
Aircraft Warning Service station, active March 12, 1942 to July 1, 1943
Will Hite says rebuilt by the DNR onto a 40-foot tower. The Register and TrailChick give 1961 and a 20-foot timber tower.
Present 14 by 14 foot DNR live-in cab on a 20-foot timber tower
Last entry in firelookout.com's list of personnel (Sandra Mosby, 1960-1961)
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on November 20, 1999 as US 362, WA 43
2015 Okanogan Complex fire (Beaver Lake fire per TrailChick) scorched the legs and burned several tower members. Accounts differ on how severe the damage was.
FEMA Public Assistance grant credited with repairs, after a contractor stabilized the tower

corrections.proposed: 14 by 14 foot flat-gable Washington DNR live-in cab
corrections.why: The L-4 cab was on the 20-foot pole tower built in 1934. The standing structure is the 1961 DNR live-in cab, which the Register and TrailChick both describe.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1934 is the L-4 pole tower. The standing cab is the 1961 DNR live-in cab (Will Hite gives 1960). The crow's nest and cabin date to 1919 per the Register and firelookout.com, or about 1911 per Will Hite and TrailChick's establishment year.
Kept 6.1 m. The Register and TrailChick describe a 20-foot timber tower. Will Hite's 40-foot figure appears once and conflicts with its own 20-foot fire section.

notes_for_editor: Summit elevation conflicts. The Register gives 6,007 ft (1,831 m), matching the record's 1830.9 m. Firelookout.com and TrailChick give 6,135 ft. Left out of facts. Access level 'restricted' is an editorial judgment from the state-land road, the DNR emergency-use cab and the usually locked catwalk. No source states a public access policy, so check with DNR before publishing. No rental found. 'Unstaffed' rests on the June 2018 Register visit report and Will Hite's 'not staffed for decades'; nothing newer. TrailChick shows a May 2026 update date, but its photos run to 2021 and its condition text predates the repairs. Will Hite contradicts itself on tower height (40 feet in the 1960 entry, 20 feet in the fire section). Photos on firelookout.com and TrailChick were not traced to a licence, so none added. The record's 'L-4' design is only the 1934 cab.
